title: Harness cp949-guard: non-CP949 chars in Write
desc: Blocks the Write tool when content contains characters that do not round-trip through CP949 (Windows Korean codepage), which would corrupt the file on a CP949 console. Use ASCII or Hangul, or route via wkedit.
steps: TRIGGER: fires on the Write tool when the content fails a CP949 round-trip (encode then decode does not equal the original). Common cause: smart quotes, emoji, or mixed CJK that the legacy codepage cannot represent.

FIX: keep source ASCII-only (code/comments) or plain Hangul; for content that must hold other glyphs, route through wkedit (UTF-8-safe, .bak backup) or delegate via Agent.cmd --model haiku. UTF-8 is canonical storage -- CP949 is only a compatibility gate.

WHY: a CP949 round-trip failure means a downstream CP949 console or tool will mojibake the file. See: ps-script-mojibake-is-output-encoding-first-not-argv, korean-argv-cp949-hell-with-wkappbot-from-bash, wkedit.
author: claude
